property_summary: The nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrant calls, so any reentrant attempt during Collect will fail in the original but succeed in the mutant.
A second call to Collect cannot execute in the same transaction, because the nonReentrant modifier locks the contract.
Once Collect enters execution, reentering Collect in the same transaction always reverts.

After any sequence of calls through Collect, the MinSum variable must remain unchanged because Collect does not modify it; the buggy nonReentrant_ modifier allows reentrant calls that can alter MinSum via SetMinSum before Collect finishes updating state.

For any account, if a Collect call succeeds, MinSum must be unchanged immediately after the call returns, because Collect itself never modifies MinSum; the buggy nonReentrant_ modifier allows SetMinSum to be called reentrantly during a Collect call that calls back into a malicious contract, letting MinSum be altered before Collect finishes.

After any call to Collect completes, MinSum must remain unchanged because Collect never modifies it and the real nonReentrant_ modifier prevents reentrant calls from changing it; the buggy modifier with an empty block allows a reentrant SetMinSum call during Collect, altering MinSum.

After any external call to Collect that does not revert, MinSum must remain unchanged because Collect never modifies MinSum and the original nonReentrant_ modifier blocks reentrant calls that could change it; the buggy empty modifier allows a reentrant SetMinSum call from a malicious contract during Collect's external call, altering MinSum.
MinSum can only be set once before initialization and subsequent attempts to change it will revert

After any sequence of calls that includes at least one call to Collect, the value of MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call to Collect, because the nonReentrant guard prevents reentrant modification of MinSum in the reference; in the buggy version where the guard is removed from the modifier, an attacker can reenter during Collect and change MinSum, violating the invariant.

After any external interaction with the contract, MinSum remains the same because SetMinSum is only callable before initialization; the buggy modified modifier loses the require(!locked_) so reentrant calls can bypass the intitalized check and change MinSum, violating this invariant.

After any call to Collect does not revert, MinSum is unchanged because the nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrant modification; the bug removes the require from the modifier, allowing a reentrant call via a malicious fallback during Collect to call SetMinSum and change MinSum.

property_summary: After any sequence of calls, MinSum can be non-zero only if the contract has been initialized; the bug allows setting MinSum before initialization.
After initialization, MinSum can be changed only by SetMinSum; the bug allows SetMinSum to update MinSum after initialization, while the reference reverts any call to SetMinSum after initialization.

For any sequence of calls, MinSum is only set to a non-zero value if the contract has been initialized (intitalized == true), but the bug allows setting MinSum to a non-zero value when the contract is not initialized.

In the reference contract, after initialization, MinSum can never be changed to a non-zero value because SetMinSum always reverts; in the buggy contract, SetMinSum can succeed after initialization and change MinSum.
After calling SetLogFile, the Log state variable's address should be immutable once Initialized is called, but the bug allows it to be overwritten by recalling SetLogFile after initialization.
After Initialized() is called, calling SetLogFile again must not change the stored Log address. The bug removes the post-init guard, allowing a second call to overwrite the Log address.
After Initialized() is called, the Log address in contract C must remain unchanged by any subsequent call to SetLogFile; the bug allows SetLogFile to overwrite the Log address after initialization.
After Initialized() is called, calling SetLogFile again with any address must not change the Log address; the bug removes the post-init guard, allowing a second call to overwrite the Log address.

After one successful call to SetLogFile, the correct contract allows a second call to change the address under the same caller, whereas the buggy contract's lock never clears so any subsequent call to SetLogFile from any caller must revert.

After a successful call to SetLogFile, the correct contract reverts on any subsequent call from any caller because intitalized remains false and the nonReentrant modifier reset is irrelevant, but the buggy contract changes the revert behavior by permanently locking the modifier; the invariant is that SetLogFile always reverts after the first successful invocation regardless of caller.

After a call to SetLogFile fails due to the method's own revert condition (intitalized is false), the nonReentrant lock must be released so that subsequent non-view calls do not revert due to the lock; the buggy version leaves the lock permanently set, causing any subsequent call to a nonReentrant function to revert.

After any successful call to SetLogFile, the nonReentrant_ lock must be reset so that a subsequent unrelated mutable function (e.g., SetMinSum) can succeed; the bugged version leaves the lock permanently true, causing any later call to a nonReentrant_ function to revert.

After a non-revert call to SetLogFile, a subsequent call to SetMinSum (or any nonReentrant_ function) must succeed; the buggy version leaves the lock permanently true, causing the next nonReentrant_ call to revert.
After any call to Initialized(), the public state variable intitalized becomes true in the reference contract, whereas the buggy contract leaves it false.

For any address that first calls Initialized() and then calls SetMinSum with any value, the reference contract reverts (because intitalized is true), whereas the buggy contract succeeds with a non-zero value (because intitalized stays false).
After any invocation of Initialized(), the intitalized state variable must be true in the reference contract, whereas the mutant incorrectly leaves it false.
After any call to Initialized(), the public state variable intitalized must return true in the reference contract, whereas the mutant incorrectly leaves it false.
